machine.admission_transition: NotAdmitted is the only entry in the sequence of a program refused at preflight admission. It is produced by the host's admission step, not by a rule program, and no rule can follow it.
machine.evaluation_order: A rule program runs its instructions in array order. `eval`, `eval_each_left_to_right`, `eval_fields_left_to_right`, `eval_to_temporary`, and `eval_selected_body` activate the rule of each operand node, depth first and left to right. `branch` pops a Boolean, activates the operand its `true` or `false` field names, runs that arm's join drops, and continues with the next instruction; its fields name operands, not labels. `branch_loop` pops a Boolean: when true it activates the operand its `true` field names, drops that operand's value, and continues with the next instruction; when false it transfers to the label its `false` field names. `jump`, `branch_catch`, `branch_callable`, and `branch_fiber` name labels, and each transfers to the instruction carrying that label in the same program. `end_catch`, `decline_catch`, `complete`, `fail`, and `protected_terminal` end the activation themselves, so an instruction placed after one of them runs only when a label transfer reaches it.
machine.join_drops: The static pass annotates each `if` arm, `match` arm, `try` body, and handler arm with the bindings another path moved and this one did not. The machine drops them, most recent binding first, as that path ends: after `branch` activates an arm, in `drop_scope` after the arm's binders and scrutinee are released, in `pop_handler`, and in `end_catch`. A `try` activation that is left abruptly drops the bindings its body moves, if still initialized, before its catch clauses are tested.

completion.value: The activation ends at `continue`, or at `end_catch` for a catch clause, having pushed exactly one operand above its entry height. A catch clause that declines ends at `decline_catch` having pushed nothing.
completion.none: The activation ends at `complete_without_value` with the operand stack at its entry height.
completion.never: The activation always ends in an abrupt transfer.
completion.terminal: The activation ends the execution with one terminal transition.

triggers.node: Activated when a resolved AST node of this form is evaluated.
triggers.machine: Activated by another instruction or by the machine driver, never by evaluating a node of its own.

unwinding: An abrupt transfer leaves activations innermost first. Each activation it leaves first drops its abandoned operand temporaries most-recent-first, then runs every cleanup record it registered, last registered first.

A guard runs when its reason is `exit`, when its reason equals the exit class of the transfer, or when its reason is `failure` and the exit class is `cancel`; other guards are discharged without running. A binding or field record drops its value if the place is still initialized.

A failure raised by cleanup while the exit class is `success` replaces the transfer and becomes the primary failure; the remaining records then run with exit class `failure`. A failure raised by cleanup while the exit class is `failure` or `cancel` is appended to the primary outcome's suppressed list and unwinding continues.

A `try` activation removes its handler before its catch clauses run. Clauses are tested in source order with F-DYN-CATCH; the first that matches completes the `try` with its body's value, and when all decline the original envelope continues unwinding unchanged.

A `while` activation consumes a loop transfer raised inside its body: edge `exit` resumes at its `exit` label and edge `continue` at its `continue` label. A loop transfer never crosses a callable, fiber, or guard boundary.

A callable frame consumes a frame transfer after running its own parameter cleanup. Edge `return` yields the value to the caller. Edge `tail-call` discards the frame and enters the new callee in its place, so the frame count does not grow. An adopted value whose loan the tail call passes on is not dropped with the frame; the new frame adopts it.

Protected edges are consumed only by a fiber step, which consumes the handle and propagates the edge, or by the execution root, which activates F-DYN-PROTECTED. An uncaught Raise at the root activates F-DYN-FAIL; a root result activates F-DYN-COMPLETE.
Suspension at `await_correlated_resume` or `suspend_to_stepper` runs no cleanup; the suspended execution keeps its cleanup stack until it is resumed or reaped.

`linearize_spawn` is one atomic step: it moves the callable into a fresh child execution, publishes the sole handle, and makes the child runnable. A failure in `reserve_scheduler_slot` precedes it, creates no child, and leaves the callable an abandoned operand of the parent. The child's grant is the parent's live grant intersected with host child policy, which is the set of grants the host allows any child of this execution to hold. In the full language the callable's declared capability row is a third term of that intersection; the executable core has no effect rows and does not model it.

The reference machine uses one admissible schedule: a child first runs when its handle is joined and then runs to its terminal. A Raise or protected edge that ends the child propagates from the join after the child's own cleanup. Dropping a handle whose child has not finished transfers the child to the reaper in cancellation-requested state; `cancel` of a child that never started drops its callable without running it.

static_obligations.end_conflicting_loans: The checker has already proven that no loan conflicting with the replacement is live; execution does nothing here.
static_obligations.validate_no_borrow_from_destination: The checker rejects a right-hand result that borrows from the destination; execution only asserts it.
static_obligations.apply_ownership_modes: Parameter modes are resolved statically. Execution materializes a borrowed temporary and asserts that no stealing parameter receives a loan and no tail call passes a loan of the frame it discards.

machine.commit_rule: Only Complete commits VM-local mutation; a request or event is appended to the journal before its Await or Emit transition is exposed.

invariants: A rule activation ends in exactly one way: its declared completion, or an abrupt transfer (Raise, protected edge, loop transfer, or frame transfer).
Every registered cleanup record runs or is discharged exactly once, in reverse registration order, before control leaves the activation that registered it.
A cleanup failure is primary only when no failure or cancellation is already active; otherwise it is suppressed and never replaces the primary outcome.
Assignment does not change its destination until its right-hand side is fully evaluated and validated.
A tail call runs the current frame's cleanup, discards that frame, and only then enters the callee; the frame count is unchanged.
A fiber step consumes the old handle and returns at most one successor; a returned, raised, or protected step returns none.
A request or event is in the journal before the Await or Emit that exposes it, and a resume is delivered at most once per request.
Exactly one terminal transition ends an execution, and no transition follows it.
